lines: Use the shared operating contract first:
Inherit the shared operating contract and consume the outputs from cards `pc_0001` through `pc_0015` if they exist.
Author the authoritative privacy, retention, cache, session, and runtime-hardening pack for the Taxat system.
This is not a generic “security checklist.” The source algorithm defines quantitative survivability thresholds,
retention-limited explainability, replay-safe preservation, cache-isolation law, session/token handling, native purge behavior,
and release-gate hardening requirements. Your job is to convert those scattered contracts into one implementation-grade,
machine-readable boundary pack that application, platform, security, privacy, and compliance agents can all rely on.
Source algorithm grounding you must honor:
`Expiry and limitation behavior`, `Quantitative survivability and privacy-preserving projection`,
`Erasure and legal-hold workflow`, `Privacy and minimization defaults`,
`Retention and privacy event requirements`, `Proof-bundle retention semantics`,
`Retention-state to error-state binding`, `Gate and progression coupling`,
`Identity, session, and command trust`, `Secret, key, and token handling`,
`Service-to-service and network hardening`, `Data protection, privacy, and cache safety`,
`Supply-chain and build integrity`, `Operational security release gates`, and `Security invariants`.
wherever upload scanning, step-up, cache purge, restore privacy reconciliation, or release gates are tightened further.
Every artifact or control row must capture at minimum:
1. Build a single artifact-retention matrix covering manifests, decisions, provenance, proof bundles,
upload-stage artifacts, collaboration artifacts, audit events, telemetry, caches, native hydration state,
authority transport envelopes, exports, and any other persisted artifacts named by the corpus.
2. Extract the quantitative privacy model exactly, including:
along with when those formulas gate progression or explanation quality.
3. Build the retention-limited explainability pack so later agents know how to remain honest when information is minimized,
4. Build a threat-to-control map spanning browser, native, API, service-to-service, cache, build pipeline, secrets, tokens,
transport, storage, and operational release gates.
5. Build an exact session / secret / token storage matrix that distinguishes:
- native Keychain or equivalent device-local storage,
- forbidden locations such as browser localStorage for sensitive bearer material.
6. Build a cache partition and purge matrix covering browser, server, object, queue, and native layers.
Explicitly call out what is reusable, what is partition-scoped, what is current-only, and what must be purged on step-up,
tenant switch, authority rebinding, session revocation, or rebase.
7. Build the restore privacy reconciliation matrix so restore/DR work cannot accidentally reopen environments before privacy and
8. Implement `validate_retention_security_pack.py` to prove coverage of artifact classes, formulas, threat classes,
purge triggers, session/token locations, and release gates.
- Close the “retention, erasure, replay preservation, and privacy limitation rules are not in one place” gap.
- Close the “quantitative survivability and fidelity formulas are hard to operationalize” gap.
- Close the “cache partitioning and purge rules are split across browser/native/security docs” gap.
- Close the “session, token, and secret handling boundaries are distributed and easy to violate” gap.
- Close the “restore privacy reconciliation is underspecified in day-to-day implementation plans” gap.
- Retention-limited artifacts may still need to support audit-sufficient explanation; minimization is not permission for silent ambiguity.
- Proof bundles and replay basis components must remain preservable enough to support allowed replay and audit outcomes.
- Legal hold can block erasure, but it must not erase the visibility of why erasure is blocked.
- No raw authority token may live in browser state, native caches, queue payloads, or analysis artifacts outside the approved boundary.
- No queue, outbox, cache, or upload artifact may be a bearer credential by itself.
- Step-up, session revocation, tenant switch, and authority rebinding must trigger the right cache purges and token invalidations.
- Native hydration must not rehydrate stale or cross-tenant sensitive state after purge or rebase.
- Restore must verify privacy reconciliation before reopening operator workflows or customer-visible surfaces.
- Malware scanning / quarantine posture for uploads must remain explicit across retention and cache behavior.
- Release gates must include supply-chain integrity, secret handling, anti-CSRF/session posture, cache isolation, and native hardened-runtime/notarization coverage where the corpus requires them.
- Treat retention tags, threat classes, purge triggers, and release gates as typed enums or closed sets, not free text.
- Keep formulas precise and deterministic; do not silently round or simplify threshold logic without documenting it.
- Use strong schema validation and deterministic sorted outputs.
- No recommendations may contradict fail-closed session handling, anti-CSRF posture, or device-local secure storage boundaries.
- Document the practical implementation boundary for every control: what layer enforces it, when it runs, and how failure is surfaced.
- Every retained or minimizable artifact class named by the corpus must appear in `artifact_retention_matrix.json`.
- Every quantitative privacy/survivability formula and threshold must be represented with exact symbols and meanings.
- Every threat class must map to one or more concrete controls and release gates.
- Every secret, token, or session credential type must have exactly one allowed storage boundary and explicit forbidden boundaries.
- Every restore / DR reopening path must state privacy reconciliation requirements.
- A security, privacy, platform, or application agent can implement retention, erasure, cache isolation, session handling,
release hardening, and restore reopening behavior directly from your outputs without re-deriving the contract from scattered prose.
